clue.text: Book a brilliantly-coloured room

parts.note: taken as written
a study is a room for reading and writing
something brilliantly coloured might be described as dressed or painted in scarlet, a vivid red

explanation.surface: A bare description of a room decorated in vivid colours.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in a different order from the clue: 'a room brilliantly-coloured' becomes A, STUDY and IN SCARLET.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the first Sherlock Holmes novel by Arthur Conan Doyle, so it is a book title.

clue.text: A composer endlessly protecting a relative of 18

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: protecting means the shortened name surrounds the second a
endlessly means the composer's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Brahms was a German composer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician guards a family member of someone mentioned elsewhere in the puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts BRAHMS to BRAHM, and 'protecting' puts the second A inside it. 18 is REBECCA, the Biblical wife of Isaac.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Abraham is the father of Isaac, so he is father-in-law to Isaac's wife.

clue.text: It could make one extremely tiddly, with rum in

definitions.text: It could make one extremely tiddly, with rum in

indicators.note: in means the word for rum is placed inside
extremely means the outer letters of the word tiddly are taken

parts.note: rum means odd, strange

explanation.surface: A warning that a drink laced with rum could leave you very tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the first and last letters of 'tiddly', T and Y; 'in' puts ODD between them. The whole clue also describes the drink, made with spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot toddy is a drink of spirits with hot water and sugar, which could make you tipsy.

clue.text: What might bring corrupt lad to vice?

definitions.text: What might bring corrupt lad to vice?

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or altered, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking what could lead a depraved young man into sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' rearranges LAD TO VICE. Read whole, the clue describes the hedonistic sweet life that tempts a young man astray.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian phrase for a life of luxury and self-indulgence, which might tempt a young man to sin.

clue.text: Island on one side of Atlantic

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
taken as written

indicators.note: side of means one edge of the word Atlantic, its first letter

explanation.surface: A geographic note about an island lying off one coast of the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona is a small island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland, famous for its abbey.

clue.text: Fixes, with sailors, device to secure wheel

parts.note: to set something is to fix it in place
a ship's crew is its sailors

explanation.surface: Fastens, with help from the crew, a gadget holding a wheel in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A small screw used to hold a wheel or collar firmly on a shaft.

clue.text: Eliza's retained a bit of brass for dress

indicators.note: retained means the Cockney phrase holds the extra letter inside it

parts.note: Eliza Doolittle, the Cockney flower girl of Pygmalion, drops her aitches, so 'had on' becomes 'ad on

indicators.note: a bit of picks a single letter from the word brass, here its second

explanation.surface: A girl kept a small brass ornament to wear with her frock.
explanation.walkthrough: Eliza Doolittle in Shaw's Pygmalion speaks Cockney, so 'had on' (was wearing) is 'AD ON; R from 'brass' goes inside, before the N.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress something up is to decorate it, a direct synonym for embellishing.

clue.text: The Globe should do this for an inspection

definitions.meaning: a globe is spherical, so it ought to have a circular appearance
a quick survey of a place

explanation.surface: Suggests a visit to Shakespeare's Globe theatre for a tour.
explanation.walkthrough: The Globe suggests the London theatre; here it is simply a ball-shaped thing, which should look circular.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a quick tour of a place to examine it is a look-round.

clue.text: Essay I record, included within collected works

indicators.note: included within means I and the record go inside the word for essay

parts.note: to essay is to attempt, to try
taken as written
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: An essay and a journal are part of an anthology of writings.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of three related novels or plays forms a connected group of works.

clue.text: Colourful contribution to an astronomical score

definitions.text: Colourful contribution to an astronomical score

parts.words: Colourful contribution to an astronomical score
parts.note: Holst's suite The Planets is a score about heavenly bodies; one movement depicts the ruddy world named after the god of war

explanation.surface: A vivid passage written for a huge musical work.
explanation.definitionFit: Mars, the subject of the first movement of Holst's The Planets, is popularly known by its rusty colour.

clue.text: Rounded mouldings, first part of work on circle

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: a circle is the shape of the letter O
the first part of a multi-volume work is volume one, abbreviated VOL I

explanation.surface: An architect describes curved decorative trim and the start of a job on a round building.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovolo is a convex quarter-round moulding in classical architecture; this is its plural.

clue.text: Boisterous girl's call for attention boy returned

parts.note: hoy is a shout used to attract someone's notice

indicators.note: returned means the boy's name is read backwards

parts.note: Ned is a boy's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A rowdy girl shouts to get noticed once a boy has come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns NED into DEN. The 's after 'girl' stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomboyish, rowdy young woman has long been called by this old-fashioned term.

clue.text: Production plan thus includes reworking of Racine

indicators.note: includes means the word for 'thus' holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: so means thus, in this way

indicators.note: reworking signals the letters of the dramatist's name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A theatre plan involves adapting a play by the French dramatist Racine.
explanation.walkthrough: Racine was a seventeenth-century French tragedian, so 'Production' and 'reworking' suggest staging his play; 'reworking of' is the anagram signal and 'includes' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: An outline of the plot of a film or play, used to plan its production, is a synonym.

clue.text: Miles in front of an insect is another

indicators.note: in front of says the abbreviation comes before the next piece

parts.note: an ant is an insect
taken as written

explanation.surface: Puzzled remark that a mile ahead of one insect there is a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the single word 'another': the clue has already mentioned one insect, and the answer is a second.
explanation.definitionFit: A praying mantis is an insect, so it is another one following the ant in the clue.

clue.text: No partners are fair to women

parts.note: taken as written
North and South are partners at the bridge table
to exist is to be, so 'are' gives exist

explanation.surface: A complaint that the absence of partners treats women unfairly.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North and South play as partners, a convention giving N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating women equally rather than discriminating against them by gender.

clue.text: Plant found in area seized by part of Roman army

indicators.note: seized by means the abbreviation is held inside the army unit

parts.note: a century was a unit of about a hundred soldiers in a Roman legion

explanation.surface: A plant is discovered in territory captured by Roman soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Centaury is a small pink-flowered herb of the gentian family, so it is a plant.

clue.text: Tries term after marks moved up in part of college year

indicators.note: in a down clue moved up means a letter shifts to an earlier position

parts.note: the phrase whose letters are reordered
M stands for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A student attempts a term once grades have been raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved up' takes the M from the end of TRIESTERM and shifts it earlier, after TRI, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A term of about three months, especially in American college calendars, is one third of the year.

clue.text: Prepare to fire at ducks and another bird

parts.note: to cock a gun is to ready it for firing
taken as written
a duck is zero in cricket, shaped like O, so ducks are two Os

explanation.surface: Ready the gun to shoot at ducks and at a second bird too.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so it gives the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockatoo is a crested parrot, so it is a bird after the ducks of the surface.

clue.text: Goes crazy — operates satisfactorily after a minute

indicators.note: after says the word for 'satisfactorily' comes behind A and M

parts.note: a machine that runs operates
OK means satisfactorily, all right

explanation.surface: Someone loses control just as a machine starts working properly after a minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operates satisfactorily' reads as one unbroken phrase, but 'after' splits it: the A and M for 'a minute' go before the word for 'satisfactorily'.
explanation.definitionFit: To behave wildly and out of control is an idiom meaning to go crazy.

clue.text: Scott's heroine reappearing in later novel

definitions.meaning: the Jewish heroine of Walter Scott's Ivanhoe
Daphne du Maurier's 1938 novel, published long after Scott's

explanation.surface: A heroine from Walter Scott turns up again in a more recent book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reappearing in' is the link: the same name returns as the title of a twentieth-century novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both a character in Ivanhoe and the title of Daphne du Maurier's novel.

clue.text: Common sense as part of know-how is dominant

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Practical judgement is said to be the most important element of expertise.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts at the W of 'know-how' and continues through 'is' and 'dom' of 'dominant'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound practical judgement gained from experience is a close synonym for good sense.

clue.text: Top officer as post-war planner one left out

indicators.note: out means the letter is removed from the planner's name

parts.note: George Marshall devised the Marshall Plan for rebuilding Europe after the Second World War
L is the abbreviation for left, and only one of the two is removed

explanation.surface: A senior commander described as the architect of post-war recovery, minus one item.
explanation.walkthrough: MARSHALL has two Ls; 'one left out' removes just one.
explanation.definitionFit: A field marshal or air marshal is among the highest military ranks.

clue.text: Worker caught, trapped by phony musclemen

parts.note: a worker bee is the standard crossword worker

indicators.note: trapped by means the abbreviation sits inside the word for phony

parts.note: fake means phony, not genuine
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A labourer is caught out by fraudsters posing as strongmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for muscular men displayed for their physiques, especially in photographs.

clue.text: Little room available to band for large instrument

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery
a band or ring is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A small room is offered to a group of musicians for a big instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks like a group of musicians; here it is a ring, the letter O. 'available to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cello is a large bowed string instrument played between the knees.

clue.text: After short time, anaesthetic that restricts movement

indicators.note: after says the anaesthetic comes behind the abbreviation

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
ether was an early general anaesthetic

explanation.surface: A patient briefly under anaesthetic can hardly move.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope or chain tying an animal to a post, limiting how far it can roam.

clue.text: Having had a close shave? Not so dangerous

definitions.text: Having had a close shave? Not so
definitions.meaning: someone who has not shaved closely is bristly
a ... situation is a frightening, risky one

explanation.surface: Someone narrowly escapes harm, though it was less perilous than it seemed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close shave' suggests a narrow escape, which fits 'dangerous'; the first definition takes it literally and denies it.
explanation.definitionFit: Unshaven means covered in hair, and slang uses the same word for scary or risky.

clue.text: Fourth part of score taken for the rest of the musicians

definitions.meaning: a score is twenty, and a quarter of that is a number

definitions.text: taken for the rest of the musicians
definitions.meaning: musicians say 'take ...' for a short break

explanation.surface: A section of a musical score is given to the other players.
explanation.walkthrough: A score here is twenty, not music; 'take five' is jazz musicians' slang for a short break.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty divided by four gives this number, and a break is to take that many minutes.

clue.text: Using both taps, I'll cool off

parts.note: taps are marked C for cold and H for hot
the apostrophe is dropped, giving the letters I, L, L

explanation.surface: Advice to run hot and cold water together before letting something cool.
explanation.walkthrough: On British taps C means cold and H hot, so 'both taps' gives the two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To chill something is to make it colder, a direct synonym for lowering its temperature.

clue.text: Relating to prime? 29 or 31, perhaps

definitions.meaning: one's prime is the peak of adult life, roughly around the age of thirty
ages just either side of thirty are approximately that number

explanation.surface: A maths puzzle about prime numbers, of which 29 and 31 are examples.
explanation.walkthrough: 29 and 31 are both prime numbers, so the surface invites a number-theory reading; here they are ages, and 'prime' is the prime of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Being about thirty years old describes someone in the prime of life, such as an age of 29 or 31.

clue.text: Could he show movement of early star or moon?

definitions.text: Could he show movement of early star or moon?

indicators.note: movement signals that the letters of the phrase following are rearranged

parts.note: fifteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Wondering whether some official could track the motion of heavenly bodies at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement of' rearranges EARLY STAR OR MOON. The whole clue is also the definition: this royal official studies the motion of stars and moon.
explanation.definitionFit: The holder of this honorary British post is an eminent scientist of the heavens, who would chart celestial motion.
